clue.text: This buccaneer built fires all over the place

indicators.note: scattered all over the place, so the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A pirate is seen setting fires everywhere he goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges the ten letters of BUILT FIRES. 'This' points to the answer itself as the pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: A filibuster was originally a freebooter, a pirate raiding Spanish colonies in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Excellent brandy…

definitions.meaning: ... is a French term for a good-quality brandy, as in ... champagne

explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this clue to the next, but each stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine means first-rate, and is also the name for a superior French cognac.

clue.text: … telephone message to pay visit to pub

indicators.note: one piece is added to the other, so the call follows the pub in the answer

parts.note: a local is your regular neighbourhood pub
to call is to pay a visit

explanation.surface: Someone phones to suggest dropping in at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain your local is the pub nearest home; 'to' means one piece is attached to the other, here following it.
explanation.definitionFit: A local call is a telephone conversation within one's own area, cheaper than a trunk call.

clue.text: Fish-bar right inside

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right goes inside the word for a bar

parts.note: a beam is a long bar of wood or metal

explanation.surface: A fish bar with something right inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Swimmer with deep voice?

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
bass is the lowest male singing voice

explanation.surface: Asks whether a swimmer has a low-pitched voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea bass is a marine fish, so a creature that swims.

clue.text: Part-pierced nobleman given decoration

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour worn as a decoration

explanation.surface: A lord receives a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part-pierced' reads as a description but is the definition: the body part often pierced for an earring.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy lower lobe of the ear is the body part most commonly pierced for jewellery.

clue.text: Polite cough from Noah, embarking

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Noah clears his throat politely as he boards the ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is the throat-clearing sound made to attract attention discreetly.

clue.text: His Excellency, put up, is commonly overwrought

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

explanation.surface: An ambassador who has been put up somewhere is in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PUT into TUP. 'is commonly' signals that the answer is a colloquial expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is informal for agitated or worked into a state of anxiety.

clue.text: Dressing for springtime, Annie so excited!

parts.note: May is a month of spring

indicators.note: excited suggests agitation, so these letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Annie is thrilled about what to wear in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges ANNIE SO into ONNAISE. 'Dressing' suggests clothing, but it is the salad kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is an egg-and-oil sauce used as a salad dressing.

clue.text: Instrument muted, con moto?

indicators.note: moto is Italian for motion, as in the musical marking con moto, so the letters are set in motion

explanation.surface: A musical instrument muted but to be played with movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con moto' is a musical direction meaning with movement; here 'con' is fodder and 'moto' moves the letters of MUTED CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A document is a legal instrument, a formal written deed.

clue.text: Henry is in pleasant alcove

indicators.note: the letter for Henry is placed in the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry is enjoying a nice spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess in a wall, an alcove.

clue.text: Bearing reliable, it is fit to take up

parts.note: air is one's bearing or manner
worthy means dependable, of good standing

explanation.surface: A reliable bearing that is fit for use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take up' means fly, so 'fit to take up' is said of an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft is airworthy when it is safe and fit to fly.

clue.text: Quiet backache? Some writers are full ofit!

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: Writers complain of a quiet bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: The writers are pencils, filled with graphite.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is graphite, the black lead in pencils.

clue.text: A French writer let out of cage

parts.note: un is French for a
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A French author releases a caged bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpen is to release from an enclosure.

clue.text: Discharge of car compound

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, so AB, able-bodied seaman
a solution is a compound of substances dissolved together

explanation.surface: A sailor's chemical discharge.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed reads 'car', but the wordplay needs 'tar', a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is the formal release or discharge from guilt or sin.

clue.text: Hounds found in black holes at Gleneagles, perhaps

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a golf hole played two under par, as might be scored at the Gleneagles course

explanation.surface: Dogs turn up in dark holes on a Scottish golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: Gleneagles is a famous golf resort in Scotland; an eagle is two strokes under par on a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Beagles are small hunting dogs, a breed of hound.

clue.text: Bounty"-big ship approaching point

parts.note: large means big
SS stands for steamship
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A large ship nears the headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity, or gifts handed out freely.

clue.text: Complex girl to choose a painter

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A girl with issues selects an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Electra complex, named after the Greek heroine, is a girl's attachment to her father.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra, the daughter of Agamemnon, gave her name to a psychological complex.

clue.text: Handling with care?

parts.note: the whole clue describes managing someone gently, and also the care a doctor gives

explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the way one handles a person, and medical care.

clue.text: Crude container used by West Indian players…

definitions.meaning: a barrel for holding crude petroleum
Caribbean steel bands make their pans from old barrels

explanation.definitionFit: An oil drum holds crude petroleum, and cut-down drums became the steelpans of Trinidad.

clue.text: As an underground hazard, the name is changed

indicators.note: the letters of the words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A danger below ground is renamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is firedamp, the explosive gas that endangers coal miners.

clue.text: … and this lady player needs good delivery

definitions.text: … and this lady player needs good delivery

parts.words: … and this lady player needs good delivery
parts.note: follows the players of the previous clue; a woman performer needs to speak her lines well

explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a female performer on stage, who must deliver lines clearly.

clue.text: Beer held upright for Bartholomew, for instance

indicators.note: the word for an upright is held within the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a post is an upright pole

explanation.surface: A man keeps his beer standing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartholomew was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.

clue.text: Peacemakers expected to be extravagant

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, keeps the peace
due means expected, as a train due at noon

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers are expected to overdo things.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive, beyond what is warranted.

clue.text: Birds in pairs in the field?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a pair is two scores of nought, each a duck

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is a field game; a batsman out without scoring makes a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks are waterbirds, and in cricket a duck is a score of zero; a pair is two in one match.

clue.text: Reflections which can be realised?

parts.note: musings in the mind, which may later be made real or merely realised by the thinker

explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts are reflections or ideas, things one can realise.

clue.text: Gloomy crypt

explanation.definitionFit: Grave means solemn or sombre, and is also a burial place.

clue.text: Tarry rope

definitions.meaning: a supporting rope on a ship's mast

explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain, and a stay is a rope bracing a mast.

clue.text: Constant as an insect's metamorphosis

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a transformation, so the letters change form

parts.note: the possessive spelling supplies the final S as a letter

explanation.surface: Something as unchanging as an insect undergoing transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metamorphosis' rearranges AN INSECTS. The surface clashes because metamorphosis is change, the opposite of constant.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means unceasing, continuing without pause.

clue.text: Drink right on one's toes

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone drinking while poised on tiptoe.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on one's toes is to be watchful and ready.

clue.text: So retiring in the city? Curious!

indicators.note: the reversed word sits in the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: NY is New York, the city

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Being shy in a big city seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' sends the short word backwards and 'in' places it within the abbreviation for New York; 'the city' here is not London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosy means inquisitive, prying into others' business.

clue.text: Religious leader turns out every Lent, in so devoted a manner

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
turns out means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchman emerges every Lent with great devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious leader' looks like a vicar, but it only gives the opening letter; 'turns out' rearranges the letters of the two words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverently describes acting with deep respect and piety.
